How to read the numbers

cells.text: People needed minus people signed up or attended
Anything above zero within three days gets a personal message, not another group email
Attended shifts against no-shows; Check in means more than one no-show in four shifts
Call and ask if the schedule still works before taking them off shifts
Training rows for that volunteer not marked done
No one works alone with open safeguarding or safety training

text.text: A good first month decides whether someone stays for years. Keep it short, specific and warm.
Week 1: welcome
Reply to the application within three working days and offer a short call.
Move the volunteer to Onboarding and add their training rows from the Training table.
Pair them with a named buddy for the first two shifts.
Week 2 to 4: practice
They shadow a shift, then run a task with the buddy beside them.
Ask after each shift what felt confusing. Fix the confusing thing for the next person.
When training is done and two shifts are attended, press Mark active.
Not a fit
If the role is wrong, offer another one before saying goodbye. If nothing fits, thank them and set the stage to Retired with a note.
A shift runs well when the lead arrives first and everyone leaves knowing they mattered.
Before people arrive
Open the shift row and read the sign-up list
Print or open the task list and the contact sheet
Set up the space, tools and sign-in sheet
When they arrive
Greet each person by name
Brief the team on the plan and any safety points
Pair new volunteers with someone experienced
At the end
Press Mark attended on each sign-up and type the hours given
Press Mark no-show for anyone who did not come or call
Thank everyone before they leave
Note anything that needs fixing before the next shift
People stay when they are noticed. Recognition costs little and should never be skipped.
A simple calendar

cells.text: Within 24 hours of a first shift
A thank-you note listing hours given
An appreciation event with the whole team

text.text: Spotting people who drift
Open the Volunteers table and sort by Reliability. Anyone showing Check in gets a call this week.
Look for active volunteers with no shifts in the last 60 days.
Ask what would make the next month easier, then act on the answer.
